cells.role: response probe: if q9 and q0 sit inside 2x the seed floor of each other, the model ignored the code and its resolution is moot

bands.read: a per-clip quality code still buys something on top of caption rotation
rotation already supplies whatever Q was providing; Q is redundant here
conditioning on a per-clip code while the caption rotates measurably hurts

decision_rule.cross_arm_rule: K=10 beats K=3 only if their q9 CLAP differ by more than 0.0084. Inside that band the ablation's answer is that Q resolution does not matter on a rotating caption pool, which is itself the finding -- it is not reported as a win for either arm.
decision_rule.metric: MusicCaps 5521 / MeanFlow 25 / CFG 0 / seed 42 / NoMask / full precision / --quality_level 9, clap_score
decision_rule.q_response_rule: |q9 - q0| <= 0.0084 means the code was ignored. That verdict is read BEFORE the cross-arm comparison: two arms that both ignore their code cannot be ranked by resolution.
decision_rule.reporting_rule: the four AES metrics are reported alongside CLAP against the same 2x-floor rule; margins under 2x a floor are ties, never wins
decision_rule.seed_floor_source: CFG0 training-seed floors as recorded in mf_dedup_quarter_contract.json

dependencies.note: 049 does not gate on 048. The NoQ quarter control that both arms are read against is produced by 048 Step 0; if 048 never runs, 049's number is still valid but has to be read against the full-scale NoQ number (0.2221) with the scale caveat attached.

known_caveat: S1-Q never trains q_embed[10] (memory: project_q_null_token_never_trained_bug). Stage 2's MeanFlow CFG target uses q=10 as its unconditional code, so both Q arms carry the same untrained-null contamination. Shared across K=3 and K=10, so it does not confound the resolution comparison, but it does mean neither absolute number is cleanly comparable to a NoQ arm without this caveat stated.

q_level is a property of the CLIP (agreement among the captioner's n captions), not of the rotated caption. A clip whose three captions disagree carries the same code whichever of them is drawn this epoch. That is the only way the two knobs can be crossed at zero extra encoding cost, and it is an assumption, not a measurement.
S1 100k = 3.18 epochs, so the rotation reaches 3*(1-(2/3)**3.18) = 2.19 of 3 captions per clip. Inherited from every other quarter rotation arm and internally budget-matched.

The bucket grid's signal is Qwen n-caption mean_similarity. project_mean_sim_interpretation_hypothesis and reference_p7v1_q_support_gating both argue this is a coarse support-set marker rather than a quality measure, so a null result here is evidence about resolution, not about quality conditioning in general.

primary_comparator.quarter_number: produced by 048 Step 0; does not exist at authoring time

hypothesis.prior: c2p0 slot0 with K=3 balanced Q reached CLAP 0.2126 at FULL scale on a single, fixed caption; 013 true-random NoQ reached 0.2221 at the same scale without any Q. Those two differ in both knobs at once, so neither licenses a prediction here. The naive read is that a rotating caption pool already regularises the text side and a per-clip code adds little, in which case K=3 and K=10 land on top of each other.
hypothesis.question: Does the RESOLUTION of the per-clip quality code matter when the caption attached to that clip rotates every epoch -- and does the code buy anything over NoQ at all?
hypothesis.single_substitution: arm = 013 true-random rotation + Q(k10_balanced); control = 013 true-random rotation + NoQ
